items.explanation: List only the columns you need; avoid SELECT * in production queries.
items.example: SELECT product_name, unit_price FROM products LIMIT 5;
items.expected: 5 rows with product name and price.

items.syntax: SELECT expr AS alias FROM t
items.explanation: AS names a computed column. Use double quotes for spaces or capitals.
items.example: SELECT product_name AS name, unit_price * 1.1 AS price_with_tax FROM products LIMIT 5;
items.expected: 5 rows with columns name and price_with_tax.

items.explanation: Removes duplicate rows from the result, across all selected columns.
items.example: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers ORDER BY country;

items.syntax: ORDER BY a ASC, b DESC
items.explanation: Sorts by a, then by b inside ties of a.
items.example: SELECT country, city, customer_id FROM customers ORDER BY country, city DESC LIMIT 10;
items.expected: 10 customers sorted by country, then city descending.

items.explanation: Skips m rows then returns n. Always pair with ORDER BY for stable pages.
items.example: SELECT order_id, order_date FROM orders ORDER BY order_id LIMIT 5 OFFSET 10;

items.syntax: CASE WHEN cond THEN x ELSE y END
items.explanation: Returns the first matching branch; NULL when nothing matches and there is no ELSE.
items.example: SELECT product_name, CASE WHEN unit_price >= 50 THEN 'premium' WHEN unit_price >= 20 THEN 'mid' ELSE 'budget' END AS band FROM products LIMIT 8;
items.expected: 8 products with a price band label.

items.syntax: SELECT a * b AS total FROM t
items.explanation: Expressions are evaluated per row. Cast to numeric before division to avoid integer division.
items.example: SELECT order_id, product_id, unit_price * quantity * (1 - discount) AS line_total FROM order_details LIMIT 5;

items.explanation: COUNT(*) counts all rows, including rows with NULLs.
items.example: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders;
items.expected: One row: the number of orders.
